title: A saturated unconfined system can be ordered so that it stays saturated and the small model is closed
source_title: The elementary theory of free Steiner triple systems

proof_spans.label: the complete author proof of the labelled lemma, retained line for line

standard_prerequisites.name: Saturated model
standard_prerequisites.statement: A structure of cardinality kappa is saturated when every type over a subset of smaller cardinality is realised in it.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the hypothesis and part of the conclusion, now for an expanded language.

standard_prerequisites.name: HF-ordering with a given initial segment
standard_prerequisites.statement: Every unconfined system carries an HF-ordering having a prescribed elementary submodel as an initial segment.
standard_prerequisites.use: It supplies the ordering the construction starts from.

standard_prerequisites.name: Expansion by constants for the small model
standard_prerequisites.statement: Adding names for the elements of the small elementary submodel to the language preserves saturation of the expansion.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the observation that lets the author pass to a saturated model of the expanded theory.

core_obligations: Take an HF-ordering of M having A as an initial segment and note that the expansion of M by names for the elements of A is still saturated (source line 930).

Pass to a saturated model of the same expanded theory of cardinality kappa and, for every element of A that is not a product of two smaller elements, use the sentence expressing that fact to ensure that the two models agree on which elements of A are products (source line 930).
Combine the ordering of the saturated model with the agreement on A to obtain an ordering of M in which A is closed and M remains saturated in the expanded language (source lines 930-931).

proof_roadmap.step: Start from an ordering with A initial and pass to a saturated model of the expanded theory.
Use the sentences isolating the non-products of A and transfer the saturation back.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled lemma at source lines 926-928: for a saturated unconfined system M of cardinality kappa, an elementary submodel A of smaller cardinality, there is an HF-ordering of M such that M stays saturated in the language expanded by that order and the closure of A under the order is A itself. The proof (source lines 929-931) is a back-and-forth style construction that the statement does not hint at: it starts from an HF-ordering with A as an initial segment, observes that expanding by names for A preserves saturation, passes to a saturated model of the expanded theory of the same cardinality, and uses the sentences that single out the elements of A which are not products of smaller elements in order to conclude that the two expansions are equivalent; only then does the ordering transfer back.
